chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥasan, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAmr, from his father ʿAmr ibn Ibrāhīm al-Hamadānī, he raised the hadith and said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: There is no harm in a man performing salat (prayer) while a fire, a lamp, and an image are before him. Surely, the One for whom he performs salat (prayer) is nearer to him than that which is before him.
So this is an anomalous narration with a disconnected sanad/isnad, and it is to be understood as a kind of concession, even though what we mentioned previously is preferable.

key_terms.الرُّخْصَةِ: a concession or dispensation in legal practice
key_terms.السِّرَاجُ: lamp or light source in front of the person praying
key_terms.الصُّورَةُ: image or figure before the worshipper
key_terms.شَاذَّةٌ: anomalous; a report regarded as irregular
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicates permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) with a fire, lamp, or image in front of oneself?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling about performing salat (prayer) while fire, a lamp, or an image is in front of the worshipper. It states permissibility, while the compiler notes that the report is anomalous and disconnected in chain, and thus treats it as indicating a concession rather than the preferred practice.
